span.term: The nonquasiregularity degree simultaneously generalizes quasiregularity and the closed pseudocharacter, so a single inequality in nq(X) specialises to both Šapirovskiĭ's regular-space bound and Sun's Hausdorff bound.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The new cardinal function nq(X) is not defined for every topological space, so the main bound does not apply universally.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A compact T1 space is exhibited for which the invariant fails to exist.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The nq(X) factor cannot simply be dropped: examples are given where the plain bound fails.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The two classical bounds this paper unifies had complicated proofs that were quite different from one another, which is the gap the paper exists to close.
span.note: what this limits: the relation between Sapirovskii's density bound and Sun's cardinality bound before this paper: Sun's proof is described as a complicated closing-off argument quite different from the proof of the density bound, so the two results were not visibly connected
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The class of spaces the theorem covers is named after the invariant being defined on them, so membership is settled by whether the quantity exists rather than by a topological property.
span.note: what this limits: the scope of the main theorem: it applies to nq-spaces, and a space is an nq-space precisely when nq(X) is defined, which is why a compact T1 example without the invariant falls outside it

span.label: nonregularity - AS A DEGREE RATHER THAN A DICHOTOMY: instead of a space being regular or not, the paper introduces a cardinal measuring HOW nonquasiregular it is, and the classical bound then holds for every space with that degree as a factor
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: quasiregular - THE HYPOTHESIS WEAKENED ONCE BEFORE IT WAS MEASURED: the classical result was stated for regular spaces, then observed to need only quasiregularity and not even Hausdorff, and only afterwards replaced by a degree
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the degree - SMALL FOR THE SPACES THAT MATTER: nq(X) is countable when the space is quasiregular and bounded by the closed pseudocharacter when it is Hausdorff, which is what stops the new factor from making the bound vacuous

span.label: The density of any space for which the nonquasiregularity degree is defined — in particular every Hausdorff space and every quasiregular space — is at most πχ(X) times c(X) times nq(X).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In a Hausdorff space the new cardinal invariant stays small, being bounded above by the closed pseudocharacter.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The single bound yields one common proof of Šapirovskiĭ's density bound for regular spaces and of Sun's cardinality bound πχ(X)c(X)ψc(X) for Hausdorff spaces, which previously had unrelated proofs.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: It follows that the cardinality of any Hausdorff space is at most πχ(X)c(X)nq(X)wψc(X), which improves Sun's bound because wψc(X) never exceeds ψc(X) in Hausdorff spaces.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The number of regular open sets of an nq-space is likewise bounded by πχ(X)c(X)nq(X).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In a Hausdorff space the nonquasiregularity degree is bounded above by the Lindelöf number.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Hence Lindelöf Hausdorff spaces form a new class, beyond the quasiregular ones, satisfying Šapirovskiĭ's inequality d(X) ≤ πχ(X)c(X).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Two spaces are exhibited, one of them Urysohn, whose density strictly exceeds πχ(X)c(X), showing the extra factor nq(X) cannot be dropped from the bound.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The nonquasiregularity degree is not defined for every space: the cofinite topology on an infinite set is compact and T1 yet has no nq(X).
